reviews.authors: Andrew Calcan, Jordan Collard, Alberto De Marchi, Scott B. Lindstrom
reviews.title: Resolvent Moreau identities without monotonicity: theory and applications to Gabay duality, Douglasâ€“Rachford and ADMM
reviews.scope: Primary abstract, Section 4.1 equations and discussion, Figure 2 including rendered PDF page 9, and selected Section 6.1 discussion. Not a complete review of the general duality proofs.
reviews.finding: The authors exhibit a six-cycle and conjecturally chaotic orbiting in a two-dimensional nonconvex basis-pursuit dual inclusion. The operators involve an affine constraint and an inverse MCP subdifferential selection, with a piecewise formula. This is direct prior evidence against claiming that chaos or periodic nonconvergence in DR/ADMM is new. The inspected example is not the present three-dimensional RAAR map of two separate spatial circles. That model distinction does not prove topological inequivalence of attracting sets.

reviews.title: On the local convergence of the Douglasâ€“Rachford algorithm
reviews.scope: Primary abstract, introduction, algorithm definition, Section 4 Theorem 3 statement and Corollaries 8â€“9. The entire geometric construction proof was not independently rederived.
reviews.finding: A spatial cylinder and double spiral produce a bounded nonconvergent DR orbit with vanishing increments and a circle of accumulation points. Thus a spatial nonconvergent geometry or a continuous limit set in DR is already known. This example does not establish a strange chaotic attractor: its accumulation circle lies in the common constraint intersection and in the fixed-point set.

reviews.finding: Interval Newton/Krawczyk inclusion is a standard validation method. The present work applies this established method to the specific periodic-orbit equations; it does not introduce a new verification theorem.

reviews.authors: Predrag Cvitanović, Roberto Artuso, Ronnie Mainieri, Gregor Tanner, Gábor Vattay
reviews.title: Chaos: Classical and Quantum
reviews.scope: Header, Section 4.7 Liouville formula, Sections 5.3–5.5 relevant multiplier/conjugacy identities and return-map qualification inspected in primary indexed PDF. Not the entire 1153-page book.
reviews.finding: Periodic-orbit organization, flow multiplier +1, positive ODE solution-map determinant and smooth-conjugacy invariance are established facts. Their application to the certified R1051 seven-cycle gives a narrow exclusion of a smooth fixed-time ODE-map equivalence, not a new chaos mechanism or universal inequivalence theorem.

claim_boundary: The additional bounded search did not locate this exact spatial-circle configuration, its selected periodic-orbit certificates or an explicit equivalence. Neither absence from these search results nor visual difference proves novelty. Period doubling is an established mechanism. The four certified simple minus-one multiplier events alone do not prove nondegenerate flips, an infinite cascade or chaotic attraction.
